chunks: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub from Muhammad ibn Yahya from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from al-Husayn ibn Sa'id from Hammad ibn Isa from Abdullah ibn al-Mughira from Abdullah ibn Sinan, who said:

I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) saying regarding a man who married his slave-girl, who was the mother of his child, and then the man died, so his son inherited her, and the son had a share in the wife of his mother. Then the child (the son) died. Does his mother inherit him? He said, 'Yes.' I said, 'When she inherits him, what does she do, while he is her husband?' He said, 'She divorces him, and he has no authority over her, and he is her slave.'

key_terms.أُمَّ وَلَدٍ: Mother of a child (from a slave father)

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling when a mother inherits her son who is also her husband in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* clarifies the unique status of a *Umm al-Walad* who is married to her master, illustrating how the master-slave bond persists even when she inherits her master's son. Imam al-Sadiq (AS) specifies that upon inheriting the son, she must effect a divorce (*faskh*) to sever the marital tie, after which the son remains her slave, highlighting the distinct legal mechanics of manumission and inheritance in Shia jurisprudence. This ruling underscores the principle that the maternal relationship and the marital relationship are separate legal entities that can coexist but require specific procedural separation for inheritance to be fully realized.
